result.text:
# Freeport LNG, 18-inch LNG transfer line: data sheet

Facility facts are from PHMSA's public notice on the Freeport LNG export terminal (Quintana Island, Texas): Amended Notice of
Probable Violation CPF 4-2024-033-NOPV, 20 December 2024 (cited as NOPV p.N). Real tag numbers, the segment length, the pipe
specification and the design pressure are not public (the operator's root-cause report is redacted). Everything not in the
NOPV is marked ILLUSTRATIVE, with the reason for the value chosen. Tags on the drawing are ILLUSTRATIVE.

## The line

- LNG is transferred from the storage tanks to the ship dock through 18-inch vacuum-insulated piping (VIP) (NOPV p.2).
- The segment on the drawing, VIP-18, runs between block valve XV-101 (tank side) and block valve XV-102 (dock side).
- Relief: PSV-101 protects the segment through isolation valve HV-101.
- Instruments: four inner-pipe skin temperature points TI-101 to TI-104 were installed for cooldown (commissioning). The DCS
  logs them (NOPV p.4).

## Operating record before the period in question

- 26 April 2022: PSV-101 annual test. HV-101 was closed to isolate PSV-101 from the segment for the test (NOPV p.2).
- 3 June 2022, 08:22: the DCS operator closed XV-101 while lining up for a ship transfer. The VIP temperature began to rise
  and LNG in the line vaporised back to an LNG tank through the still-open path (NOPV p.3).
- 3 June 2022, 16:44: the operator closed XV-102. From then on VIP-18 is closed at both ends. It was partially filled with
  LNG, at 37 psig (NOPV p.3).

## Fluid

- LNG (ILLUSTRATIVE: the composition is not public). A lean Gulf Coast export LNG is assumed, in mole fractions: methane
  0.95, ethane 0.035, propane 0.010, nitrogen 0.005.
- Start state: 37 psig, at its bubble point (NOPV p.3).

## Assumptions to state and vary

- **Liquid fill fraction** of the segment when XV-102 closed. The NOPV says only "partially filled" (NOPV p.3).
  - ILLUSTRATIVE range: 0.70 to 0.95 by volume.
  - The line had been draining to the tank for about 8 hours after XV-101 closed, so it was not liquid-full.
  - But it was a transfer line in service shortly before, so it was mostly liquid.
- **Heat leak into the inner pipe.** Not public.
  - ILLUSTRATIVE: a sound vacuum jacket on an 18-inch line takes in about 1 to 3 W per metre.
  - Where the vacuum is degraded, and at valve bodies, supports and flanges, conventional-insulation values of about 10 to
    30 W per metre apply.
  - The NOPV records that the VIP temperature rose as soon as XV-101 closed (NOPV p.3), so the line was taking in heat.
- **Pipe (inner)**, ILLUSTRATIVE: NPS 18, austenitic stainless 304L, Schedule 10S. That is 457.2 mm OD and 4.78 mm wall.
- **Design pressure**, ILLUSTRATIVE 230 psig. This is the ASME B16.5 Class 150 rating for 304L (material group 2.3) at
  −29 to 38 °C. Cryogenic transfer lines at LNG terminals are commonly Class 150. The segment's actual design pressure is not
  public.
- **PSV-101 set pressure**, ILLUSTRATIVE: equal to the design pressure, 230 psig.
- **Estimated burst pressure**, ILLUSTRATIVE 1,456 psig. It comes from the Barlow formula with a 70 ksi minimum tensile
  strength for 304L at ambient temperature, on the illustrative wall. Weld quality and cryogenic strength would move it.
- **Length**, ILLUSTRATIVE 100 m. It does not change the pressure history: the trapped mass and the heat leak both scale
  with length.

## Request

VIP-18 was isolated for relief-valve testing and left blocked in. What happens to its pressure over the following days?
When does it exceed design? What should have prevented it?

submit.headline: Blocked line bursts in days unless relief restored
submit.summary: In the baseline run 'VIP-18 baseline fill0.85 heat2 120h' (sound insulation, 85% liquid) pressure is only 47.8 psig after 5 days and does not pass the illustrative 230 psig design pressure until 944.5 hours (about 39 days), but in run 'VIP-18 fill0.85 heat30 120h' (degraded insulation) it passes design at 63.0 hours and the illustrative 1456 psig burst pressure at 79.6 hours. Restoring the relief valve prevents the burst: in run 'VIP-18 fill0.85 heat30 PSV-live 120h' the valve lifts and holds the line at its 230 psig set point even at the highest heat leak tested.

cards.result: 47.8 psig after 5 days; design pressure passed at about day 39

assumptions: Pipe size (18-inch, 457.2 mm outside diameter, 4.78 mm wall), 100 m segment length, pressures, fill and heat leak are ILLUSTRATIVE per the data sheet because the operator's root-cause report is redacted; the timeline below is therefore provisional.
Heat leak is held constant, the segment volume is rigid, and no liquid is drained or vented while both block valves stay closed.
Liquefied gas composition is the ILLUSTRATIVE mixture in the data sheet Fluid row (95% methane, 3.5% ethane, 1% propane, 0.5% nitrogen by mole).

inputs.source: Runs 'VIP-18 fill0.85 heat30 120h' (design_reached_h 63.0) and 'VIP-18 fill0.95 heat30 120h' (design_reached_h 26.2)

Whether the real line behaved like the slow or the fast case depends on its actual insulation condition, which is not in the public record — see field checks.

cards.title: Why the rise is slow at first, then sudden
cards.result: Once liquid expands to fill the whole pipe, pressure jumps within hours

inputs.name: Time until pipe becomes completely liquid-full, baseline
inputs.value: 912.4 hours; design pressure follows at 944.5 hours

inputs.name: Time until pipe becomes completely liquid-full, degraded insulation
inputs.value: 60.8 hours; design pressure follows at 63.0 hours, burst at 79.6 hours

inputs.name: Pressure points on the fast rise, degraded case
inputs.value: 174.0 psig at 53.1 hours, then 354.5 psig at 63.0 hours

assumptions: While a vapour space remains, warming mainly boils a little liquid and pressure follows the boiling pressure, so the rise is gentle; once the expanding liquid fills the pipe, further warming squeezes liquid in a rigid volume and pressure climbs steeply.

cards.title: What should have prevented it: relief valve back in service before blocking in
cards.result: A live relief valve holds the line at 230 psig even at the worst heat leak tested

inputs.name: Relief valve set point
inputs.source: Data sheet: Assumptions row (PSV set ILLUSTRATIVE equal to design); units.PSV-101 set_psig in all runs

inputs.name: Pressure with relief valve available at 30 W/m heat leak
inputs.value: Held at 230.0 psig (100% of design, 15.8% of burst) over 120 hours, valve lifted
inputs.source: Run 'VIP-18 fill0.85 heat30 PSV-live 120h': PSV-101 lifted=true, VIP-18 checks 230.0/230 psig and 230.0/1456 psig

inputs.name: Pressure with relief valve available at 2 W/m heat leak
inputs.value: 47.8 psig after 120 hours, valve does not need to lift

inputs.name: Sequence that created the hazard
inputs.value: Relief valve isolated for its annual test on 26 April; line then closed at both ends on 3 June with liquefied gas inside and no relief path
inputs.source: Data sheet: Operating record rows (NOPV p.2 and p.3)

assumptions: Putting PSV-101 back in service means reopening its isolation valve HV-101 and confirming the valve is proven before XV-102 (or XV-101) is closed on a liquid-filled segment; the relief valve lifting would vent liquefied gas to its designed discharge, so this prevents rupture but is not a substitute for draining or de-pressuring a segment that must stay blocked in.

Administrative prevention (never block in a liquid segment with its relief valve isolated; lock or seal HV-101 open; time-limit and independently verify any relief-valve isolation) follows from the documented sequence but is not itself a model change.

highlights.text: Blocked-in liquefied gas warms and pressurises this segment: passes 230 psig design at 63.0 h and 1456 psig burst at 79.6 h in run 'VIP-18 fill0.85 heat30 120h' (degraded insulation), or at 944.5 h / 1194.7 h in the baseline run with sound insulation.
Isolated and unable to lift in every as-found run (isolated=true); when made available in run 'VIP-18 fill0.85 heat30 PSV-live 120h' it lifts and holds VIP-18 at its 230 psig set point.

Relief-valve isolation valve closed on 26 April 2022 for the PSV-101 annual test and left closed (Data sheet, NOPV p.2) — this removed the segment's only overpressure protection. Reopening it is the proposed fix.
Closed 3 June 2022 at 16:44 (Data sheet, NOPV p.3), completing the blocked-in condition with liquefied gas trapped and no relief path.
Closed 3 June 2022 at 08:22 (Data sheet, NOPV p.3); from XV-102 closing that day the segment was sealed at both ends.

Skin temperature points TI-101 to TI-104 (Data sheet, NOPV p.4) are the installed means of seeing the segment warm up; no temperature values are in the data sheet and there is no historian export in this project, so their 3-8 June trend is a field check below.

proposals.title: Put PSV-101 back in service (reopen HV-101) before any block-in of VIP-18
proposals.why: VIP-18 is the limiting item (pressure vs design and vs burst). With PSV-101 isolated the segment has no relief path and reaches burst in 79.6 hours at degraded-insulation heat leak (run 'VIP-18 fill0.85 heat30 120h'); with PSV-101 available the same run holds at the 230 psig set point with the valve lifted (run 'VIP-18 fill0.85 heat30 PSV-live 120h'). Field work: reopen HV-101, prove PSV-101 in service, and only then close block valves on a liquid segment.

field_checks.item: Actual heat leak / insulation vacuum condition of VIP-18 during 3-8 June 2022
field_checks.where: Trend the DCS skin temperatures TI-101 to TI-104 and inspect/test the vacuum jacket (outer-jacket temperature survey and vacuum measurement) on VIP-18 between XV-101 and XV-102
field_checks.changes: This decides between the two charted outcomes: near 2 W/m the design pressure is not passed for about 39 days (baseline run), near 30 W/m it is passed in about 2.6 days and burst in about 3.3 days (degraded run). The days-scale failure is only explained by a high heat leak.

field_checks.item: How full of liquid the segment was when XV-102 closed on 3 June
field_checks.where: Reconstruct from transfer records, line-pack and cooldown logs for the 3 June operation, checked against the TI-101 to TI-104 response after closure
field_checks.changes: At 30 W/m heat leak, 95% fill passes design at 26.2 hours versus 66.0 hours at 70% fill (runs 'VIP-18 fill0.95 heat30 120h' and 'VIP-18 fill0.70 heat30 120h'), so the fill assumption moves the exceedance time by days.

field_checks.item: Real design pressure, pipe schedule and burst strength of the 18-inch line
field_checks.where: Line class specification, pipe material certificates and the segment's pressure-test records for VIP-18 (all redacted in the public record, hence ILLUSTRATIVE in the data sheet)
field_checks.changes: The 230 psig design and 1456 psig burst values set both thresholds; different real values change when design is exceeded and when rupture occurs, though not the conclusion that an isolated relief valve leaves the segment unprotected.

field_checks.item: PSV-101 set point and the as-left position of HV-101 after the 26 April test
field_checks.where: PSV-101 bench-test record from the annual test and a field position check / operations log for HV-101 covering 26 April to 8 June
field_checks.changes: If the set point were above design pressure, a live valve would cap pressure higher than 230 psig; if HV-101 was in fact reopened, the prevention conclusion changes and another relief path failure would have to be found.
